steps.say: Equivalent fractions are the same amount, written with different numbers.

figure.alt: A bar in 2 equal parts with 1 part shaded.

steps.say: Cut each half into 2 again. Now 2 out of 4 parts are shaded.

figure.alt: The same bar in 4 equal parts with 2 parts shaded.

steps.say: Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number to make an equal fraction.
To compare unit fractions, look at the bottom number. More parts means smaller parts.
With the same bottom number, more parts means a bigger fraction.

options.why: 2/3 is more than half: 2 out of 3 parts.

hints: Half means 1 out of every 2 parts.
For a half, the top number is half of the bottom number.

options.why: Sixths are smaller parts than quarters.
Both have 1 part, but the parts are different sizes.

hints: Both fractions have 1 part on top.
Picture a cake cut into 4 and a cake cut into 6.
check.explanation: A cake cut into 4 has bigger pieces than a cake cut into 6. So 1/4 is bigger than 1/6.
